# Complete native Web login only after the expected cookies exist

## Platform difference

When OH uses a native Web login page, Dart must receive a deliberate completion/cancellation result rather than assuming page load implies authenticated state.

## Implementation

Nomark routes OH login into an ArkTS Web page and returns cookies through an emitter event, with an empty result on exit. Its follow-up adds configured cookie URLs/key allowlists, required success keys and polling for asynchronously written cookies, and clears the timer on completion. Non-OH paths keep their existing haptics/WebView implementation.

## Applicability

The success contract must match the authentication service's actual cookies and redirects. Preserve a single owner for the request and prevent callbacks after page disposal.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Polling does not prove service compatibility or session validity. Nomark stores session/cookie keys in native preferences; do not describe that as an audited encrypted keystore.

## Verification

Test redirects, delayed cookies, user back/cancel, missing success keys, repeat logins and timer/listener cleanup; independently verify any credential-storage requirement.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
